summary: Equities pulled back from all-time highs Monday after Iran attacked the UAE for the first time since the ceasefire began, sending Brent crude surging toward $114. Now in its tenth week, the Middle East war has driven energy prices sharply higher and heightened inflation risks, with gold down roughly 12% since the conflict began as rising real yields and a hawkish Fed hold erode bullion's appeal and push safe-haven flows into equities instead.
tweet: Iran-UAE missile strike jolted oil to $114/bbl Monday, knocking stocks off highs and hammering gold — now down ~12% since the war began — as a hawkish Fed hold keeps rate cuts firmly off the table.
